reason: PR #79 (#72), d499d4bedc2caf3c83cad1cf4dcb2511c2ecd19f: initialization instructions and recall description add provisional memory guidance only. Exact full diff retained for review; no schema, tool, response, or default changes accepted.

+      "instructions": "Use assemble_context for task context with a non-empty query and scope={\"project\":\"golden-wire\"}; k defaults to 3 (recommend k<=3). In default gated mode, set needs_memory=true when prior context is needed or prior_failure=true after a failed attempt; both default to false. Closed gates inject zero tokens. Operator modes are gated, always_on, and off. Recall only for explicit need, prior failure, or ambiguity that memory can resolve; map ambiguity to needs_memory=true. Request k<=3 and prefer relevant verified fix-span records. This guidance is provisional pending representative coding evaluation (#74); fixture calibration alone does not establish efficacy. Keep recall for explicit memory search; its default k=10 is unchanged. Correct one input error and retry once. If the tool is unavailable or fails again, report memory pre-flight unavailable.",

-          "description": "Hybrid BM25 + dense + graph recall from CRYSTALIUM memory. Returns slot-budgeted, redacted CrystalSummary records. Universally allowed (all tiers). Rate-limited (200 calls/min). scope.project is required; CRYSTALIUM never guesses a cross-project scope. Use scope={\"project\":\"golden-wire\",\"agent_class_visibility\":\"vigil\"}. explain=true (v1.6) adds a diagnostic `explain` object to the result so a zero-record recall against a non-empty store is diagnosable without a separate `doctor` call. v1.9.0 (crystalium#36): query relevance is the primary composition signal \u2014 `k` is a hard cap on the number of returned records, and records are emitted in non-increasing `score` order (id ascending tiebreak). Every record carries a non-null `score` and the response always carries a `budget` object (total_cap, slots, k_requested, k_applied, truncated_count). Revertible to the pre-1.9.0 behaviour via Config.recall_relevance_primary=false. v1.10.0 (crystalium#38): `score` is now a WEIGHTED hybrid-retrieval RRF fusion value (previously unweighted) \u2014 ordering semantics are unchanged (still non-increasing, id-ascending tiebreak) but the magnitude and the relative order among candidates can differ from 1.9.0. The graph and completion arms are collapsed into one correlated derived voter and the sparse arm receives a query-conditional selectivity boost; explain=true additionally surfaces a `fusion` object (per-arm weights + the selectivity inputs that produced them). Revertible via Config.recall_weighted_fusion=false (subsumed under recall_relevance_primary \u2014 either flag off restores the unweighted fusion).",

This guidance is provisional pending representative coding evaluation (#74); the API default remains 10. Universally allowed (all tiers). Use scope={\"project\":\"golden-wire\",\"agent_class_visibility\":\"vigil\"}. explain=true (v1.6) adds a diagnostic `explain` object to the result so a zero-record recall against a non-empty store is diagnosable without a separate `doctor` call. v1.9.0 (crystalium#36): query relevance is the primary composition signal \u2014 `k` is a hard cap on the number of returned records, and records are emitted in non-increasing `score` order (id ascending tiebreak). Every record carries a non-null `score` and the response always carries a `budget` object (total_cap, slots, k_requested, k_applied, truncated_count). Revertible to the pre-1.9.0 behaviour via Config.recall_relevance_primary=false. v1.10.0 (crystalium#38): `score` is now a WEIGHTED hybrid-retrieval RRF fusion value (previously unweighted) \u2014 ordering semantics are unchanged (still non-increasing, id-ascending tiebreak) but the magnitude and the relative order among candidates can differ from 1.9.0. The graph and completion arms are collapsed into one correlated derived voter and the sparse arm receives a query-conditional selectivity boost; explain=true additionally surfaces a `fusion` object (per-arm weights + the selectivity inputs that produced them). Revertible via Config.recall_weighted_fusion=false (subsumed under recall_relevance_primary \u2014 either flag off restores the unweighted fusion).",
